- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast moderately, especially if recent prices are rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5–10% above prior peak.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of 30d window); adjust downward if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history includes multiple high/low swings, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of smoothing or delay in peak detection.
- When sentiment is consistently positive but prices are flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to correct; apply early correction rule based on sentiment shift.
